title: Equipment Setup and Artifact Removal for Simultaneous Electroencephalogram and Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging for Clinical Review in Epilepsy
protocol: Mark electrode positions on the patient's scalp, based on the 10-20 system.
Measure and note the patient's head center line of the scalp by placing a measuring tape from the nasion to the inion by passing the top center of the head (Measure A: sagittal plane).
Mark 50% of Measure A from the nasion to the inion. This mark indicates the electrode's Cz location.
Mark 10% of Measure A from the nasion to the indicated Cz. This mark indicates the electrode's Fpz location.
Mark 10% of Measure A from the inion to the indicated Cz. This mark indicates the electrode's Oz location.
Mark 20% of Measure A from the indicated Cz to Fpz. This mark indicates the electrode's Fz location.
Mark 20% of Measure A from the indicated Cz to Oz. This mark indicates the electrode's Pz location.
Measure and note the patient's head from the left preauricular point to the right preauricular point by passing the top center of the head (Measure B: coronal plane).
Mark 50% of Measure B and make sure this location is overlapped with the indicated Cz location.
Mark 10% of Measure B from the left preauricular point to Cz. This mark indicates the electrode's T3 location.
Mark 10% of Measure B from the right preauricular point to Cz for T4 location.
Mark 20% of Measure B from Cz to T3 for C3 location.
Mark 20% of Measure B from Cz to T4 for C4 location.
Measure and note the circumference of the patient's head by passing through Fpz and Oz (Measure C: transverse plane).
Mark 10% of Measure C left and right from Fpz for Fp1 and Fp2 locations, respectively.
Mark 10% of Measure C left and right from Oz for O1 and O2 locations, respectively.
Mark 20% of Measure C left from Fp1 and right from Fp2 for F7 and F8 locations, respectively.
Measure the distance from F7 and F8 in the coronal plane (Measure D: coronal plane).
Mark 50% of Measure D to overlap with previously indicated Fz.
Mark 25% of Measure D from F7 toward Fz and from F8 to Fz for F3 and F4 locations, respectively.
Measure the distance from nasion to inion passing through Fp1 and O1 to ensure 50% overlaps with C3.
Measure the distance from nasion to inion passing through Fp2 and O2 to ensure 50% overlaps with C4.
Clean the patient's scalp using skin prep gel on gauze.
Place conductive paste on one electrode cup.
Place the electrode on the patient's scalp following the channel name on the electrode's cable.
Repeat placing the gel and electrodes on the patient's scalp for all electrodes.
Adhere electrodes to the patient's scalp using glue on gauze.
Arrange electrode cables and place cable junctions far from the scalp by placing pads of gauze on the center of the subject's head.
Wrap all cable junctions with self-adhesive bandage wrap.
Place an elastic head cover to secure all the electrodes.
Connect the harness, which is connected to the electrodes, to the amplifier.
Begin monitoring EEG synchronously with video recordings.
Connect the USB 2 adapter to the Triggerbox kit in the monitoring room using a thick white cable.
Connect the Syncbox to the USB 2 adapter using a thick black cable.
Connect one end of the fiber optic cable to the Syncbox in the monitoring room.
Pass another end of the fiber optic cable through a tunnel connected to the scanning room.
Connect a USB port cable from the USB 2 adapter to the recording computer.
Connect a USB port cable from the Syncbox to the recording computer.
Connect a USB port cable from the Triggerbox to the recording computer.
Connect the software license dongle to the recording computer.
Set up the EEG recording amplifier along with the MR-sled kit inside the scanner.
Remove any metal or MR-sensitive components from the experimenters.
Charge the amplifier battery prior to conducting the recording.
Turn on the amplifier and connect the end of the fiber optic cable in the scanning room to the back of the amplifier.
Open the EEG recording software by clicking the software icon on the computer screen.
Create a workspace in the recording software by clicking the New Workspace menu under the File tab.
Set a folder path where new data will be stored by clicking the Browse button.
Insert the data name in the Prefix blank box and specify the numbering index for Min. Counter Size [digits] and Current Number.
Confirm that the file name is correctly displayed under Next Resulting Filename, then click Next.
Scan the amplifier by clicking the Scan for Amplifier button.
Set up appropriate parameters including sampling rates and low and high cut-off frequencies for recording.
Select a Sampling Rate of 5000 Hz to sufficiently sample gradient artifacts from the scanner.
Insert a Low Cutoff of 10 seconds to prevent direct current (DC) saturation.
Set a High Cutoff of 250 Hz to limit the gradient artifact amplitude before entering the analog-to-digital converter.
Transfer the patient to the scanning waiting room.
Explain the recording procedure to the patient.
Clean the patient's back, right below the left shoulder where the ECG lead will be placed.
Apply an abrasive electrolyte gel on the ECG lead and place it on the left back side of the patient.
Apply adhesive tape around the ECG lead and cable to minimize scanning artifacts during the recording.
Disconnect the EEG harness and connect the EEG cable junctions to the interface box.
Transport the patient to the scanning room.
Lay the patient down onto the scanning table with the head in the open bottom half of the head coil.
Support the patient's back when lying down.
Apply earplugs to help reduce the scanner's noise.
Apply a cushion around the patient's head to minimize head movement artifacts.
Connect the top half of the head coil to close the "bird cage" coil around the patient's head.
Adjust the bed height.
Connect the interface box to the amplifier.
Place MR-safe sandbags around the cables to minimize the MR artifacts during the recording.
Communicate with the patient through a microphone in the monitoring room, explaining that additional steps for setting the software settings are being carried out.
Check the impedance of the EEG electrodes by clicking on the Impedance Check button in the recording software window.
Confirm with the patient that they are ready for the recording.
Start the EEG recording by clicking on the Play button in the recording software.
Run the fMRI acquisition scan.
Open the EEG analysis software.
Apply MR artifact correction.
Click on the Transformations > Special Signal Processing > MR Correction tab.
When a small window is generated, select Use Markers.
Choose a trigger signal from the scanner and click Next.
Select the Interleaved and Based on Time options.
Insert the time information of the trigger signal.
Click on Next.
Enable Baseline Correction for Average.
Uncheck Compute Baseline Over the Whole Artifact.
Insert Start [ms] and End [ms] values.
Select Use Sliding Average Calculation.
Insert Total Number of Intervals for Sliding Average.
Check Common Use of All Channels for bad Intervals and Correction.
Select Use All Channels for Correction.
Click Next.
Check Do Downsampling.
Choose 500 for New Frequency [Hz].
Check Apply Lowpass Filter.
Select Use FIR Filter.
Insert 70 for Cut-off Frequency [Hz].
Click on Next.
Select one Store Corrected Data option.
Click on Finish.
Apply DC removal by a high-pass filter.
Click on the Transformation > Data Filtering > IIR Filters tab.
Check Enabled under Low Cutoff.
Insert a cutoff Frequency [Hz] of 0.5.
Choose the filter Order as 2.
Click on OK.
Remove cardioballistic artifacts.
Click on the Transformations > Special Signal Processing > CB Correction tab.
Select Use Peak Detection and check Semiautomatic Mode.
Under the Search Pulse Template section, insert Start[s] as 60.
Insert Length[s] as 20.
Check Mark Found Template and make sure the appropriate ECG channel is chosen.
Insert proper parameters for Pulse Rate and Correlation and Amplitude.
Insert R for Mark Pulses with R-Peak Markers.
Click on Next.
Check Use Whole Data to Compute the Time Delay.
Insert Total Number of Pulse Intervals Used for Average.
Move all EEG channels except the ECG channel to the right column under Correct Following Channels.
Select one Store Corrected Data option as preferred.
Click on Finish.
Slide over the time axis at the bottom of the Navigation Bar in the CB Correction-Interactive Mode window.
Check where the base template ECG is highlighted with a blue shaded box.
Confirm the base template of the ECG is correctly marked.
Double-click the ECG channel name to display only the ECG channel for review.
Consider manual adjustment of the peak or interval as needed.
In the CB Correction-Interactive Mode window, check each marked ECG by double-clicking on its corresponding row in the table.
Adjust detected peak locations as needed by moving red vertical lines.
Once all detected ECGs are reviewed, click on Finish.
